subject: Mutual plan & conversion terms — MAP milestones, PoC credit request
messages:
From: Sara Price <sara@acmeanalytics.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Mark Thompson <mark.thompson@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from yesterday's call

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. We loved the throughput profile and the KV cache example — it maps nicely to our ingestion window. Before we spin up a pilot, the procurement team asked for a short mutual action plan that maps milestones to success criteria and the credits you’re comfortable providing during the PoC.

Specifically we’d like:
- 8-week PoC with throughput tests (week 3) and quality evals against our benchmark prompts (week 6)
- A clear conversion pricing for 6 and 12 month committed capacity if we hit the success criteria
- A line item that confirms how Redwood will support kernel selection/quantization during the PoC

Any chance you can share a one-page MAP + a short summary of PoC credits/discounts? Procurement also asked for the draft SOW if we move to a PO at conversion.

Best,
Sara
Sara Price
Director, Data Platforms
ACME Analytics

(Attachment: example-runbook.pdf — sent separately)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Sara Price <sara@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Mark Thompson <mark.thompson@acmeanalytics.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from yesterday's call

Sara —

Great to hear — glad the demo resonated. I’ll put together a concise MAP and a proposed PoC credit schedule. High-level proposal below; I’ll follow up with a PDF and a draft SOW for procurement: 

Proposed MAP (initial):
- Week 0: Kickoff + access (Redwood sandbox, credentials, initial model config)
- Week 1–2: Integration + baseline throughput measurement (engineering check-ins weekly)
- Week 3: Throughput ramp test (target 50k tokens/min sustained)
- Week 4–5: Prompt quality tuning + quantization experiments
- Week 6: Quality eval vs ACME benchmark (pass/fail threshold: >92% of baseline on precision metric)
- Week 7: Final report + decision meeting
- Week 8: Conversion window (if success)

PoC credits / commercial ask: 
- Redwood provides $30k in platform credits to cover the pilot infrastructure.
- If ACME commits to a 6-month reserved capacity within 30 days of the decision meeting, Redwood will convert $20k of credits into a first-month invoice credit + 10% new-customer ramp discount for months 1–3.
- 12-month commit option: $30k credit converted + 15% ramp discount and a 90-day pricing guarantee.

We’re flexible on the exact numbers depending on the scope of throughput required — I proposed a middle-ground to start the conversation. I’ll run this by Marissa for approval on the credit conversion language and by Karthik for any SOW/legal constraints.

I’ll circulate the MAP_v1.pdf and a short PoC_Credit_Summary.xlsx by EOD Thu.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
D: (415) 555-0132

(Attachments to follow: MAP_v1.pdf, PoC_Credit_Summary.xlsx)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP / PoC credit proposal for ACME

Team —

Quick notes after reviewing Dylan’s draft:
- $30k credit is within standard AE discretionary range; conversion language must tie credits to measurable milestones (example: credit conversion only upon signed PO for reserved capacity or executed contract).
- Legal wants the phrase “non-refundable upon conversion” removed; instead use "applied as invoice credit on first month".
- Approve the 6-month/12-month commit tiers but restrict the 15% discount to customers with SOC2 completed or an active compliance plan — ACME flagged SOC2 in RFP; we need to check status.
- Karthik: please confirm if we can guarantee the 90-day pricing hold in the Private/Dedicated offering.

Also: include a small advisory line in the SOW about model change management — who owns model weights and who handles quantized artifacts.

Marissa
Head of Sales Ops

(Forwarded: Dylan’s MAP draft attached for comments)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP / PoC credit proposal for ACME

Marissa/Dylan —

I confirm: we can offer a 90-day pricing guarantee for hosted and dedicated offerings, provided the customer signs the reserved capacity clause and the SOW includes a "no model-substance changes" window for the first 60 days after conversion. I’ll task legal to add a narrow clause around quantized artifact ownership (we host artifacts; customer retains usage rights).

I also recommend adding a small pilot SLA for availability during the PoC (99% uptime target) so ACME can lock a performance expectation. That helps the procurement team feel comfortable converting credits.

Karthik
VP, Product 

(Notes: flagged SOC2 status check — outreach to ACME security team required)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Sara Price <sara@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Mark Thompson <mark.thompson@acmeanalytics.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: MAP_v1 + PoC credit summary (draft)

Sara —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are: MAP_v1.pdf (one-page mutual action plan), PoC_Credit_Summary.xlsx (breaks down the $30k credit by expected infra and engineering support), and a draft SOW skeleton (Draft_SOW_ACME.docx). Highlights:
- Pilot scope: 8 weeks as discussed.
- Credits: $30k applied to platform usage; $20k of that converts to invoice credit on month 1 if ACME signs a 6-month reserved capacity PO within 30 days of the decision meeting.
- Ramp discount: 10% for months 1–3 on 6-month commit; 15% for 12-month commit with SOC2/Compliance precondition.
- Availability: Pilot SLA 99% (we’ll provide uptime reporting in Console).

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm ACME’s SOC2 progress (procurement asked this explicitly)?
2) Schedule the kickoff — we can start as early as Jun 22 if credentials are ready.
3) Any changes to the conversion timeline we should consider?

If procurement wants a longer free trial rather than credits, we can model an extension instead, but conversion economics would shift (credits give clearer invoice reconciliation).

Best regards,
Dylan

(Attachments: MAP_v1.pdf, PoC_Credit_Summary.xlsx, Draft_SOW_ACME.docx)

From: Mark Thompson <mark.thompson@acmeanalytics.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, Sara Price <sara@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP_v1 + PoC credit summary (draft)

Dylan / Sara —

Thanks for the draft. Procurement likes the clarity of the MAP but asked two follow-ups before we sign the kickoff:  
1) Can the credit be split so that 25% of the $30k is reserved for a month-0 smoke test and is refundable if the integration fails to reach the baseline throughput? Procurement wants a safety valve.
2) Can Redwood extend the PoC window by 2 weeks (total 10 weeks) if the quality tuning phase runs long — this would be without additional credits but with an agreement that conversion pricing timeline can shift accordingly.

If you can accept (1) and (2), procurement is comfortable moving forward with the kickoff and will circulate a short PO for the conversion clause after the decision meeting. We’ll also confirm SOC2 status by next Tue.

CC’d Marissa for discount/credit approval if we adjust split.

Regards,
Mark
VP, Procurement
ACME Analytics
